notes: Owner explicitly asked to try lesson two, but 14 of the 29 canonical source introductions conflict with age/numbers scope and need owner curriculum/lifecycle rulings. All 29 source IDs and semantic roles remain authoritative; no silent relocation. Lesson one has 12 separate unresolved decisions. No TTS or actual product built.

items.label: Can recognise cardinal numbers from 11-100. (P)
items.rationale: Recognize examples of spoken cardinal numbers across 11–100 by sound, including teen/ty contrast. Real Otti/audio perception still needs external playback test.

items.label: Can understand basic questions about objects in pictures or in their immediate surroundings. (P)
items.rationale: A spoken question about numbered visible cards provides one object-in-picture comprehension check. Do not claim general object vocabulary mastery.

items.label: Can understand a phone number from a recorded message. (P)
items.rationale: Separate genuinely recorded fictional telephone message, never just the age conversation or unplayed script. Missing recorded clip blocks mastery.

items.label: Can use brief, everyday expressions to describe wants and needs, and request information. (Ca)
items.rationale: Asking about age requests familiar information in a changed situation, only partially demonstrates the broader wants/needs communicative objective.

items.label: X years old
items.rationale: The exact productive frame X years old needs a meaningful independently observed age response in a new fictional role; a heard dialogue alone cannot count.

items.label: FORM: AFFIRMATIVE INTERROGATIVE, WITH 'BE'
items.rationale: Are you nineteen? in a realistic age confirmation demonstrates affirmative be interrogative usage narrowly, not every subject/person/conjugation.

items.label: FORM: (SUBJECT) QUESTIONS WITH 'BE'
items.rationale: Who is nineteen? provides a natural who/subject question tied to two pictured ages. Verify EGP objective interpretation with source owner before claiming full grammar coverage.
